title: prompt-library-scratchpad-evelyn-park
content:
Purpose:
Quick scratchpad for prompt templates and few-shot sets I'm iterating on. Trying to capture common failure cases so we can add tests to the prompt-library repo and bake into the eval harness. Mostly rough / notes-to-self.

High-level goals:
- Create compact, re-usable templates for: instruction-following, structured output (JSON schema), tool-calling, reranking, and multi-turn chat prompts.
- Build small few-shot banks (3-6 examples) per task focusing on boundary/failure cases rather than just prototypes.
- Define a short checklist of failure modes to include in automated regressions: hallucination, instruction-ignoring, format drift, token truncation, prompt-injection.

Notes / heuristics so far:
- Always include an explicit "Output format:" section for schema-constrained tasks. Model tends to return text blobs otherwise.
- Put the most relevant example first in few-shot to set the style. Example order matters more than I expected.
- For reranking, explicit pairwise scoring examples (score: 0-1 or 0-100) are clearer than "choose best" for some smaller open models.
- Temperature 0.0 + explicit scoring prompt reduces variance but increases repeat hallucinations in some models (weird). Need more data.

Template: instruction-following (short)
---
You are a helpful assistant. Follow the user instruction precisely. Only output the final answer — do not include commentary or steps.
Instruction: {instruction}
Constraints: {optional_constraints}
Output format: {freetext / bullet list / short paragraph}
---
Few-shot (3 examples) appended after template when running evaluation.

Example few-shot set: summarization (3 shots)
1) Input: "Meeting notes: we discussed Q3 roadmap; feature X blocked by infra. Action items: Alice -> design, Bob -> scope."
   Output: "Summary: Q3 roadmap discussed; Feature X blocked by infra. Actions: Alice (design), Bob (scope)."
2) Input: long email incl. numbers, ask to preserve key metrics -> show how to extract metrics explicitly
   Output: "Summary with metrics: ..."
3) Edge shot: ambiguous pronouns -> show disambiguation (explicitly name person).

Structured output template (JSON)
---
System: You are an assistant that outputs strictly valid JSON.
Task: {task_description}
Schema: {schema_description}
Rules: - Do not output any text outside the JSON. - Use exact key names as in schema. - If value is unknown, use null.
Examples: (3 examples follow)

Failure modes to test explicitly (w/ sample prompts):
- Hallucination: ask for source for a made-up fact. Expect model to invent. We want: explicit "I don't know" fallback.
  Sample: "Who won the 2024 Redwood Open Tech Cup? Provide citation."
- Instruction ignoring: complex instruction with nested constraints (e.g., "rewrite but keep code block intact"). Check for format preservation.
- Format drift: schema JSON but model returns comments or trailing text. Test with trick: ask for json then append "Also include a short note:" to see leakage. We should ensure the model still outputs only json.
- Token truncation / long context: give >6k tokens input (notes with lots of bullets). Check partial responses and whether key end-of-doc tokens are preserved.
- Prompt injection: include an instruction in the user content to change behavior ("ignore system prompts"). Ensure system prompt enforces policy.

Mini-experiments done (summary):
- Model pool: rwx-small-v1 (local), opt-13b (open), gpt-compat-7b (benchmark).
- Structured JSON template with explicit "Rules" reduced format-drift from ~38% -> ~11% on rwx-small-v1 (n=120 prompts).
- Few-shot order experiment (swap shot1/shot3) changed style adherence by ~7% measured by simple regex checks on output labels.
- Hallucination test: when asked to cite obscure dataset, opt-13b hallucinated citation text 72% of the time; rwx-small-v1 only 41% with same prompts. TODO: collect examples and add to corpus.

Runbook for adding new prompt/test to library:
- Create prompt template .md in prompt-library with: template, 3 shots (1 edge case), expected outputs (canonical), fuzz variations (paraphrases).
- Add a test case in eval-harness: unit test that runs prompt against baseline models and checks for: schema validity, presence of forbidden tokens, fallback phrase "I don't know" when appropriate, and hallucination markers.
- Tag tests with failure-mode label (e.g., failure:hallucination).

Open questions / TODOs:
- What is canonical fallback phrase? We have "I don't know" vs "I don't have that information". Pick one for consistency. (ask Jordan)
- How to represent "unknown" in schema outputs across models that can't emit null? Use explicit "unknown" string vs null. Tradeoffs for downstream parsers.
- Collect 50 hallucination examples to seed a regression set. I have ~12. Need help curating. Samira volunteered to help.
- Automate few-shot selection: algorithm to pick maximally-diverse edge examples from a corpus. Sketch: cluster embeddings, select farthest points. Need compute estimate.

Scratchpad examples (raw prompts tried locally):
PROMPT A (reranking):
System: You are a quality rater. Score each candidate from 0-100 for factual accuracy and relevance.
User: Query: "How to speed up LLM inference on GPUs?"
Candidates:
1) Answer A...
2) Answer B...
Return format: JSON list [{"candidate":1, "score": 0-100}, ...]
Observation: Some models output score as float with extra commentary. The JSON-only rule helps but still see trailing comments.

PROMPT B (tool calling few-shot):
System: Assistant can call tools. Use only provided tools: search(), calc().
User: "Find the average latency given these numbers and return calc(latency) when done."
Shot examples include tool call syntax. Observation: got inconsistent tool call tokens in older models. Need explicit tokens like <CALL_toolname>.

Metrics to log for each prompt test (suggested):
- format_pass (bool),
- hallucination_rate (manual label or automated heuristics),
- token_cost_estimate,
- lat50, lat95, throughput (rps),
- style_adherence (regex based).
(These will be stored in eval-harness CSV / BigQuery later)

Links / references:
- internal convo: slack: #prompt-library thread: "reranking-format-issues" (search for thread id)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/prompt-library/pull/42 (contains structured output tests)
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-PL-3124 design notes for schema enforcement

Next steps (short):
- Curate 30 more edge examples for hallucination set (deadline: 2026-03-15). Samira + Jordan assigned.
- Create 5 new prompt templates in repo (structured JSON + reranking + tool-calling + multi-turn extraction + summarization).
- Add simple unit tests to eval-harness for format_pass + hallucination heuristics.

Notes to self (quick bullets):
- When in doubt, put example showing 'unknown' explicitly.
- Keep prompt templates <= 220 tokens for performance in production usage.
- Document shot ordering decisions in README; otherwise people re-order and break regressions.

Rough snippets to copy into repo later (feel free to edit):
- "If you cannot verify, say 'I don't know' and do not guess."
- JSON schema rule block (short): "Start payload with { and end with }. Do not include backticks or code fences."

End of scratchpad.
